protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; RULE-GOVERNED SATISFIED re-record of DR-115 under adopted D-056 Class B plus a D-001 MF-6 file-08 edit
reviewGrade: Offered as the dedicated SATISFIED-GRADE review D-056 Eligibility gate 4 requires for DR-115. Gates 1-3 certify; gate 5 does not certify as specified — see gatesCertified and D089-MF-1.
summary: The eligibility case for DR-115 is sound and I certify gates 1, 2 and 3 — the lead label is DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, D-006 left no undecided numbers and the register itself draws the contrast with DR-118, and D-006 assigns the exact machine pins to the G03/G04 harness-naming act rather than to DR-115. What fails is the write. The primary replacement target, the bare lead token, is not unique: it occurs on five rows, and executed as written the instruction marks DR-104, DR-118, DR-119 and DR-123 SATISFIED alongside DR-115 — two of them on D-056's ineligible list, and all four refused by this entry's own clause 5. Separately, the condition-2 rewrite deletes the named remainder D-085 installed for DR-102 and adds none for DR-115, so the readiness snapshot would show two SATISFIED rows owing nothing, in a scheme where the named remainder is part of the SATISFIED evidence.

gatesCertified.gate1_classB_DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED: CERTIFIED. The live DR-115 lead label is DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED and D-006's CONSENT digest bfd8a758… matches the entry's citation.
gatesCertified.gate2_remainder_is_only_measurement: CERTIFIED. The live cell ends 'the MEASUREMENT half is discharged at qualification under the D-006 scope disposition', and D-006 states that the harness-namer 'executes this class, never co-authors the threshold', so no threshold authoring remains.
gatesCertified.gate3_remainder_named_at_a_DR-G_obligati: CERTIFIED. DR-G01..G05 all exist with owners; G01/G02/G05 carry recorded identifiers after D-088 and G03/G04 are reserved-not-named, which is a condition-4 remainder rather than DR-115 design work.
gatesCertified.gate5_MF-6_records_SATISFIED_and_removes: NOT CERTIFIED AS SPECIFIED. The Blueprint-impact displacement is correct and its target is unique, but the lead replacement names a five-occurrence string and would record SATISFIED on four rows beyond this one. Gate 5 requires an MF-6 that records SATISFIED for this row; as written it does more than that.

objections.location: Subject, Decision clause 4, first bullet: 'Replace the live DR-115 lead token `**DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED**` with `**SATISFIED 2026-08-14 (D-089 / D-056 Class B).**`'
objections.claim: The replacement target is not unique. It occurs five times in file 08, and the instruction executed as written marks four additional rows SATISFIED — including two that D-056 lists as ineligible and all four that this entry's own clause 5 refuses.
objections.why: I counted occurrences before reading what the entry intended, as I do for every byte-exact target in this corpus, and `**DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED**` returns five: DR-104 at line 286, DR-115 at 297, DR-118 at 300, DR-119 at 301 and DR-123 at 305. That count is not incidental — it is the same five the live condition-2 cell reports as '5 `DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED`'. A literal string replacement therefore rewrites all five lead labels to 'SATISFIED 2026-08-14 (D-089 / D-056 Class B).' The consequences are the most serious this corpus admits. DR-104 and DR-118 are on D-056's ineligible list — 'DR-103/104/105/114/118 and the twelve no-contract rows remain ineligible' — so they cannot be SATISFIED under this instrument at all. DR-119 and DR-123 are eligible in kind but not performed, and D-056 gate 4 requires each to have its own dedicated SATISFIED-GRADE review, which neither has had. The entry contradicts itself in the process: clause 5 says 'Does not mark DR-103/118/119/123 SATISFIED', and the condition-2 rewrite counts '4 `DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED`' remaining, which is arithmetic that only holds if exactly one row flipped — if the instruction were executed as written the correct count would be zero. So the entry's own numbers presuppose a single-row edit while its instruction names a five-row string. The entry does supply a disambiguator, 'After the new lead, the next words remain `— thresholds DECIDED 2026-08-13 (D-006:`', and I verified that phrase occurs exactly once. But it is phrased as a post-condition describing what survives, not as part of the string to be matched, and it appears after the replacement instruction rather than in it. Every comparable target in the two adopted siblings is unique on its own: I verified each of D-085's five anchors at count 1 across three turns, and D-088 keyed its twenty prefixes by gate ID. This is the first non-unique replacement target in the series, and the row it could corrupt most is the one that records SATISFIED.
objections.repair: Make the match itself unique. Replace `**DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED** — thresholds DECIDED 2026-08-13 (D-006:` with `**SATISFIED 2026-08-14 (D-089 / D-056 Class B).** — thresholds DECIDED 2026-08-13 (D-006:`. I verified that combined string occurs exactly once in the live file.

objections.location: Subject, Decision clause 4, third bullet: the condition-2 snapshot 'Measured now' rewrite
objections.claim: The rewrite deletes the named remainder D-085 installed for DR-102, deletes DR-103's accepted-contract note, and records no remainder for DR-115 — leaving the readiness snapshot showing two SATISFIED rows that owe nothing.
objections.why: The live cell, written by D-085 and adopted at 0963bebe…, reads 'DR-102 `SATISFIED` under D-056 Class A (D-085); leftover CC-1..CC-11 execution remains at DR-G21 / condition 4. DR-103 carries an independently accepted design contract (D-013) and remains `OPEN` on its fixture-corpus authoring half'. The replacement reads 'DR-102 `SATISFIED` under D-056 Class A (D-085); DR-115 `SATISFIED` under D-056 Class B (D-089). DR-103 remains `OPEN` on fixture-corpus authoring.' Three things go: DR-102's leftover clause, DR-103's design-contract standing, and — never added — any statement of DR-115's own measurement remainder. This is not presentational. D-056's operative sentence is that 'architecture SATISFIED evidence is the independently reviewed design contract or already-recorded D-000 decision plus the named remainder list.' The named remainder is constitutive of the SATISFIED, not a footnote to it, which is why D-085 put DR-102's leftover in this cell and why my turn-1 review of D-085 treated the enumeration of leftovers as the gate that could fail. A condition-2 snapshot that reports two SATISFIED rows and no remainders states that condition 2's satisfied rows carry no qualification debt, when both carry it and both route it to condition 4. There is also a consistency problem with the entry's own framing: it asserts 'This entry does not overturn those' of D-085, and clause 5 carefully protects D-088's gate-harness cells, while this bullet silently rewrites away operative text that D-085's adopted decision installed and that D-085's reversibility clause names as the thing an overturn must restore. And the pattern compounds — DR-119 and DR-123 remain eligible in kind, so on this template the fourth re-record would present four SATISFIED rows with no remainders at all.
objections.repair: Preserve the remainder list. Carry DR-102's 'leftover CC-1..CC-11 execution remains at DR-G21 / condition 4' forward, add the parallel clause for DR-115 — measurement remains at DR-G01..G05 / condition 4 — and restore DR-103's accepted-contract standing. If the coordinator instead intends remainders to live only in the row cells, that is a defensible choice but it should be decided and recorded explicitly, with D-085's text removed by a stated disposition rather than by a rewrite that does not mention it.

objections.location: Subject, Decision clause 4, third bullet: the backtick-delimited replacement text
objections.claim: The replacement text is ambiguously delimited: its inner backticks are unescaped inside a backtick-quoted block, so the byte-exact specification does not unambiguously state the bytes to write.
objections.why: The block opens with a backtick and then contains `SATISFIED`, `OPEN`, `DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED` and `PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW` with live backticks, each of which closes the enclosing span. An executor copying the text between the outer delimiters gets a truncated string, and cannot tell from the draft alone whether the written cell should contain the backticks or not. That this is a genuine deviation rather than my preference is settled by the sibling entry: I counted escaping in both files, and the adopted D-085 turn-3 draft escapes its inner backticks sixteen times, writing \`SATISFIED\` throughout the same cell's replacement text, while D-089 escapes zero. The intent is recoverable — the live cell does carry backticks and D-085 is the precedent — which is why this is not a MUST-FIX. But clause 4 is headed 'Exact file-08 edits', and an exact specification should not require the executor to infer its own delimiters.
objections.repair: Escape the inner backticks as D-085 does, or quote the replacement in a fenced block that does not rely on backtick delimiting.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, Eligibility recitation item 3: 'recorded identifiers for the countable subset'
notesNonBlocking.observation: This revives the word 'countable', which is the exact term D-086's operative rider RB-GHN-V3-A1 orders removed from v3 and around which two blockers were raised — GHN-V1-B2 and GHN-V2-B1, the latter being the invention of a smaller 'countable required' required-set. It is not a breach: the rider scopes removal to v3's remainingUnmetNamed sentence and forbids presenting 16 as the required-gate denominator, and this sentence does neither — it uses the term as a category for the three of DR-G01..G05 that received identifiers, which is accurate, since D-088 named G01, G02 and G05 and reserved G03 and G04. But v3's own refusals exist precisely to keep that word from becoming a category in the register's vocabulary, and 'the named subset' or 'the three presently recordable' would say the same thing without reopening it.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 051fbd0847559429d962a8f20adb4416b4ebd6163166b417ec2a3121159ef96e, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at ecb18cd0… across start and end.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on every row, which is worth noting given this is the third consecutive entry to re-pin after a sibling adoption. COORD 29d9fd8b…, file 08 18713a60… and the freeze e809d439… all match live bytes, and all three commits resolve at full hash: 75c981dd… to D-056, 0963bebe… to 'D-085: record DR-102 SATISFIED under D-056 Class A' and 94b28c86… to D-088. file 08 is at its post-D-085 value, so the entry is measured against the world it will be applied to.

Gate 1 verifies against live bytes and against D-006. The DR-115 lead label is `**DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED**`, which is D-056's Class B trigger, and D-006's three-turn CONSENT digest is recorded in COORD as bfd8a758…, matching the entry's citation.

Gate 2 verifies from the register's own words rather than the entry's characterisation. The live DR-115 status cell ends 'the MEASUREMENT half is discharged at qualification under the D-006 scope disposition', and D-006 states that the exact machine identifiers, OS versions and cache-state protocol 'are pinned by the G03/G04 harness-naming, which is itself a REVIEWED decision commit with product sign-off on representativeness — the harness-namer executes this class, never co-authors the threshold.' So the machine pins are condition-4 work and no threshold authoring remains at DR-115. The entry's contrast with DR-118 is also the register's own: DR-118's cell reads '**per-row thresholds remain UNDECIDED** (unlike DR-115)'.

The attack 'leftover is not only measurement — G03/G04 machine pins treated as DR-115 design' therefore fails, and the entry's phrasing that this 'is a C4 remainder, not a DR-115 design leftover' is the same split D-006 draws.

The attack 'applies the split to DR-118' fails on the entry's text — clause 5 refuses DR-103/118/119/123 and the alternative 'Include DR-118. Rejected: thresholds UNDECIDED' is present and accurate — but see D089-MF-1, where the write instruction contradicts that refusal.

Gate 3 verifies against the post-D-088 register. DR-G01 through DR-G05 all exist with owners — Release engineering, Architecture + release, Release engineering, Release engineering, Component publisher + release — and after D-088 G01, G02 and G05 carry 'named: harness.DR-G0n…' prefixes while G03 and G04 carry 'reserved, not named (D-006 machine pins owed; D-086).' That is exactly the state the recitation describes.

The condition-2 arithmetic is correct, which I established by tallying the thirty rows myself rather than trusting either cell. The live lead-label tally is 22 OPEN, 1 SATISFIED, 5 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED and 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, summing to thirty, with DR-115 leading DECIDED. Flipping DR-115 gives exactly the entry's 2, 22, 4 and 2, which also sums to thirty. The 'what that means' clause 'condition 2 remains 1 of 30 SATISFIED' is present verbatim and exactly once, so the attack 'stale 1 of 30 after C2 becomes 2 of 30' fails.

Of the four replacement targets, three are unique and one is not. The Blueprint-impact cell 'Hard blocker for falsifiable “small”; not yet QUALIFIED — the measurement half remains' occurs exactly once, curly quotes included; the next-words disambiguator occurs exactly once; the one-sentence clause occurs exactly once. The bare lead token occurs five times — D089-MF-1.

The attack 'leaves the Blueprint-impact measurement hard-blocker live' fails. The replacement removes the hard-blocker and keeps the honest residue, 'Measurement remains condition 4 / DR-G01..G05 / DR-012 qualification, not an architecture hard blocker. Not QUALIFIED.' This is the same displacement D-085 was made to perform at ADV-D085-01, and the entry cites that lineage in its rejected alternatives.

The attack 'treats measurement as architecture SATISFIED' fails: clause 2 states measurement 'is not architecture SATISFIED evidence and is not an architecture hard blocker', and clause 3 preserves D-006's numbers and runner-class decision.

The attacks 'claims QUALIFIED' and 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fail. Every QUALIFIED occurrence is a refusal or a preserved 'Not QUALIFIED' in the new cell text, the header refuses QUALIFIED and DEMONSTRATED, and both implementation references are refusals with condition 5 remaining NOT MET and last.

The attack 'overturns D-088' fails on the entry's text: the header, clause 5 and the reversibility clause each refuse it, Eligibility item 5 adds 'It does not rewrite D-088 gate-harness cells', and no gate row appears in the edit list. The readiness effect also carries D-088's condition-4 standing forward correctly at 'PARTLY MET at 16 of 18'.

The lead replacement preserves the D-006 history as claimed: the instruction keeps the remainder of the status cell, and I confirmed the words following the lead token are '— thresholds DECIDED 2026-08-13 (D-006:' so the numbers, runner classes and the MEASUREMENT-half sentence all survive in the row.
D-089 is absent from COORD, no Codex verdict exists at review time, and COORD and file 08 are unmodified in my working tree.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with two MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. The eligibility case is the strongest part of this entry and I certify three of the five gates outright — D-006 genuinely left no undecided numbers, and it is D-006 itself, not this draft, that assigns the exact machine pins to the harness-naming act, which is the distinction the whole Class B claim turns on. The failures are in the write. I count occurrences for every byte-exact target as a matter of course, and this is the first target in the series that is not unique: the bare lead token sits on five rows, and the instruction as written would record SATISFIED on four rows this entry expressly refuses and that D-056 either bars outright or requires their own reviews for. The entry's own condition-2 arithmetic proves the single-row intent, which is what makes the instruction a defect rather than a disagreement. The second failure is quieter and I nearly filed it as a note: the condition-2 rewrite drops the leftover clause D-085 installed and adds none for DR-115. Under D-056 the named remainder is part of what makes the SATISFIED lawful, so a snapshot showing two satisfied rows owing nothing is not a formatting choice. Both repairs are small and neither disturbs the eligibility case.
